title: Bounded Queue
description: Build a fixed-capacity FIFO queue on a ring buffer that refuses new items when it is full.
statement:
Implement a fixed-capacity FIFO queue, `BoundedQueue(capacity)`, as a **ring buffer**: allocate a list of `capacity` slots once and reuse them as items come and go, so nothing is ever grown, shifted or copied. A full queue refuses new items instead of growing: that is back-pressure, and the caller decides whether to wait, drop or fail.

- `offer(item)` adds `item` at the tail and returns `True`. If the queue is full it returns `False` and changes nothing.
- `poll()` removes and returns the oldest item, or returns `None` if the queue is empty.
- `size()` is the number of items inside. `capacity` is at least 1.
- Items can be anything except `None` (that is what `poll` answers for an empty queue), including `0` and `""`.

**Example**

```python
q = BoundedQueue(2)
q.offer("a")   # True
q.offer("b")   # True
q.offer("c")   # False: full, and "c" is not stored
q.poll()       # "a"
q.offer("c")   # True: the slot "a" used is free again
q.size()       # 2
```

tests.name: items come out in the order they went in
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(3)
assert [q.offer(item) for item in "abc"] == [True, True, True]
assert [q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll()] == ["a", "b", "c"]

tests.name: offer returns False when the queue is full, and the refused item is not stored
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(2)
assert [q.offer(1), q.offer(2), q.offer(3)] == [True, True, False]
assert q.size() == 2
assert [q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll()] == [1, 2, None]

tests.name: poll on an empty queue returns None, again and again
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(2)
assert q.poll() == None
assert q.size() == 0
q.offer("x")
assert q.poll() == "x"
assert [q.poll(), q.poll()] == [None, None]
assert q.size() == 0

tests.name: size follows the offers and polls, and a refused offer does not count
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(3)
sizes = []
for item in [1, 2, 3, 4]:
    q.offer(item)
    sizes.append(q.size())
for _ in range(4):
    q.poll()
    sizes.append(q.size())
assert sizes == [1, 2, 3, 3, 2, 1, 0, 0]

tests.name: a freed slot is reused: the tail wraps around to the start of the list
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(3)
for item in [1, 2, 3]:
    q.offer(item)
assert q.poll() == 1
assert q.offer(4) == True
assert q.offer(5) == False
assert [q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll()] == [2, 3, 4, None]

tests.name: a queue that fills up part-way along the list is still full, not empty
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(3)
q.offer("x")
q.poll()
q.offer("y")
q.poll()                            # the oldest item would now be in the last slot
for item in [1, 2, 3]:
    assert q.offer(item) == True
assert q.offer(4) == False
assert q.size() == 3
assert [q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll()] == [1, 2, 3]

tests.name: stays correct while the indices wrap around hundreds of times
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(3)
out = []
number = 0
for _ in range(500):
    q.offer(number)
    q.offer(number + 1)
    number += 2
    out.append(q.poll())
    out.append(q.poll())
assert out == list(range(1000))

tests.name: a queue of capacity 1
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(1)
assert q.offer("a") == True
assert q.offer("b") == False
assert q.poll() == "a"
assert q.poll() == None
assert q.offer("c") == True
assert q.poll() == "c"

tests.name: 0, "" and False are items like any other
tests.code:
q = BoundedQueue(4)
for item in [0, "", False, 5]:
    assert q.offer(item) == True
assert q.size() == 4
assert [q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll(), q.poll()] == [0, "", False, 5]
assert q.poll() == None

tests.name: behaves like a plain FIFO with a limit over 5,000 random offers and polls (capacity 4)
tests.code:
import random
from collections import deque

rng = random.Random(5)
real, model = BoundedQueue(4), deque()
for step in range(5000):
    if rng.random() < 0.55:
        item = rng.randrange(1000)
        accepted = real.offer(item)
        assert accepted == (len(model) < 4), f"step {step}: offer({item}) returned {accepted!r} while {len(model)} item(s) were inside"
        if accepted:
            model.append(item)
    else:
        got = real.poll()
        want = model.popleft() if model else None
        assert got == want, f"step {step}: poll() returned {got!r}, expected {want!r}"
    assert real.size() == len(model), f"step {step}: size() is {real.size()!r}, expected {len(model)}"

hints: A list of fixed length, used as a circle. Which two numbers tell you where the oldest item is and where the next one goes?
Keep `head` (the index of the oldest item) and `count`. The next free slot is `(head + count) % capacity`, and `poll` moves `head` forward by one, also modulo the capacity.

Track the count, not just a tail index: with only a head and a tail, a full queue and an empty queue look the same (`head == tail`). Decide emptiness from the count, never from what a slot holds, because `0` and `""` are valid items.
explanation:
**The idea.** A ring buffer is a fixed list used as a circle. Remember where the oldest item is (`head`) and how many items there are (`count`). The next free slot is `(head + count) % capacity`; the `%` makes the index wrap from the end of the list back to 0. `offer` writes there and increases `count`; `poll` reads at `head`, moves `head` forward by one (also modulo `capacity`) and decreases `count`. Nothing is ever shifted or copied, so both are O(1), whereas `list.pop(0)` moves every remaining item.

**Why keep a count.** If you track only a head and a tail index, a full queue and an empty queue both look like `head == tail`. A count (or one deliberately unused slot) removes the ambiguity.

**Why bounded.** An unbounded queue between a fast producer and a slow consumer just grows until the process runs out of memory. A bound turns overload into a signal: `offer` returns `False` and the producer can slow down, drop the work, or fail. That is back-pressure. A multi-threaded version adds a lock and condition variables (see `queue.Queue(maxsize)`); this is its single-threaded core.

**Details.** Clear the slot on `poll` so the buffer does not keep an item alive after it has left the queue. Return `None` for an empty queue before touching any slot, and do not decide emptiness by looking at what a slot holds: `0` and `""` are legal items.

**Complexity.** O(1) per call and O(capacity) memory.
